summary: Backend-only testing for the Night Finder Forgot Password flow (Resend transactional email) — POST /api/auth/forgot-password + POST /api/auth/reset-password. Created a formal pytest suite (8 test cases) covering OTP mode, magic-link mode, privacy (200 for unknown emails), rate limit (max 3 rows / 15 min), body validation (missing code+token), invalid codes, full happy-path OTP reset with subsequent login using the new password, single-use enforcement (code cannot be replayed), and identical flow for magic-link tokens. Result: 8/8 PASSED. Rate limit correctly caps persisted entries at 3 even though all 4 requests return 200 (privacy-preserving). Backend logs also confirm Resend attempted delivery — real email to onboarding@resend.dev sender was accepted for the whitelisted address and refused for others (expected behavior, does not affect logic).

minor.issue: Rate-limit window is per-email (max 3 in 15min) but does not include the used flag in the counter — after a successful /reset-password call, existing rows are marked used but they still count toward the 15-min quota (count_documents ignores 'used'). Not a security issue (user reset succeeded), but a legitimate user who resets successfully and later needs another reset will be silently blocked. Consider adding {'used': False} to the count filter.

Response includes a fresh JWT that is issued BEFORE the password hash update is reflected in the returned public_user (still uses the pre-update `user` dict). Not a bug per se — the token itself is valid — but the returned user object is the pre-update snapshot. Cosmetic only.

action_items: (Optional) Include {'used': False} in the rate-limit count_documents filter in /api/auth/forgot-password so a completed reset does not consume the 15-min quota.

(Optional) Re-fetch the user document after password_hash update before building public_user in /api/auth/reset-password (currently the returned user is the pre-update snapshot — token is still valid).
critical_code_review_comments: email_service.py correctly runs the blocking Resend SDK in a thread pool via loop.run_in_executor — good for FastAPI async handlers.
server.py password reset flow correctly uses sha256(code) as token_hash (never stores raw code), single-use via 'used' flag, and 30-min TTL via expires_at — matches security best practices.
Privacy: forgot-password intentionally returns 200 for both known and unknown emails — verified in tests.
Reset endpoint correctly invalidates all other pending resets for the same user after success (update_many with used:True) — good defence-in-depth.
seed_data_creation: Tests create a throwaway user via /api/auth/register with a random suffix and clean it up (delete users + password_resets rows for that email) in the module fixture teardown.
context_for_next_testing_agent: All 8 forgot/reset password tests pass. Test file at /app/backend/tests/test_password_reset.py is reusable — it uses EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL and MONGO_URL from env, cleans up after itself, and inserts reset rows directly into MongoDB to simulate 'user received the email'. Resend SDK will attempt real delivery on every forgot-password call but this is a no-op for the test flow (we insert the reset row manually).
